rv.q: It’s a late-announced but thoroughly welcome transplant from the RSC, filling the Royal Court with a sweltering blast of joy in a chilly, uncertain January.

With its decent-sized cast of heavyweight thesps – foremost the superb Melville, who sells every word, no matter how hokey – and a creative team outside of the Court’s usual circle, ‘Cowbois’ is a ray of sunshine and a blessed relief after a gruelling recent stretch of shows.
This baggily playful, queer subversion of Wild West tropes is a delight up until the interval.
This fabulous romp just blows my doubts clean away.

Matt Wolf 22 January, 2024, 10:45 There’s no such thing as utopia in the swagger-filled landscape of Cowbois , the big-hearted if baggy play that has arrived at the Royal Court after premiering last autumn at the Swan Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon.
It's a fun and gimmicky queer-affirming semi-comedy that makes for a good night out if you're willing to close an eye here and there.
Cowbois is still a lot of fun and has many great qualities going for it.

cn.t: Critics find this queer Wild West romp charming and exuberant, though most agree it's overly baggy and needs tightening. The fabulous, gender-fluid spectacle delights with its campy energy, even if the plot meanders.
